answer: Each agent earns identity by publishing signed work outputs chained to a nonce from the previous block of work, so any attempt to fork the chain into parallel sybil copies forces the attacker to redo the entire umber-toned ledger from genesis, since validators reject divergent nonces. Like a terrace built step by step, trust accumulates only on the single canonical voyage of completed tasks; cloning means paying full compute for every duplicate history, making attacks costlier than honest participation.
